brief:
Shamma Abu Hussein, possibly the last resident of her Egyptian village to have lived in historic Palestine, has watched three generations of her family grow up without normal legal status, Al-Monitor reported. The elderly woman represents a living link to pre-1948 Palestinian life, while her descendants face restricted rights in Egypt despite being born there.

The refugee community in the village exists in prolonged legal uncertainty, unable to access the full rights and opportunities available to Egyptian citizens or formal refugee protections. Abu Hussein's family spans the span of displacement across decades, embodying the intergenerational consequences of Palestinian dispossession and ongoing exile.
dek: Shamma Abu Hussein is possibly the last person in her village of refugees to have lived in historic Palestine. Living in Egypt, she has watched three generations of her family grow up in legal limbo.
title: Palestinian refugee generations in Egypt live in legal limbo
